summary: The Haight has closed its own street for a fair since the 1970s — the ninth was in 1986 — and closed Cole Street for political rallies since at least 1980. In 1996 the Board put interim controls on Haight Street to stop new places selling alcohol from opening. In 2005 it asked the city to look into residents repeatedly finding syringes on Cole Street, and in the same year commended the 409 House on Clayton Street for its contributions to community activism. Two of the neighbourhood's trees are landmarks in their own right: a black acacia on Masonic Avenue and a coast redwood at 313 Scott Street.
